record.notes: Dated July 2026; the ministry's call for public comments set a submission deadline of 4 August 2026, with written submissions to the Committee on Artificial Intelligence and Other Emerging Technologies. It builds on the Kenya AI Strategy 2025-2030 (KE-01), the Digital Master Plan 2022-2032 and the Data Protection Act 2019, and underwent legal review, including by the Office of the Attorney General. For systems placed into service after the policy takes effect, full compliance would be required once the relevant implementing regulations come into force; systems already in operation would have a two-year transition, and high-risk legacy systems three years to comply fully.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored: the draft policy PDF (226 pages) and the ministry's public-participation page, both from ict.go.ke (16 Oct 2026). The PDF confirms the title, the July 2026 date, the issuing ministry and state department and the provisions summarised; the public-participation page calls it a draft, invites comments and gives the deadline of 4 August 2026. The PDF's cover reads 'Kenya Artificial Intelligence and Other Emerging Technologies Policy' without the word draft, and its foreword calls it 'the Kenya AI and other Emerging Technologies Policy, 2026'. Nothing stored shows Cabinet approval, a sessional paper or a bill after the consultation. The December 2025 Implementation Roadmap of KE-01, mentioned in the earlier notes, is not among the stored files and is no longer cited.

The draft Policy subsequently underwent legal and institutional review processes.

summary.quote: This policy adopts an effects-based jurisdictional approach
Develop a dedicated AI and other Emerging Technologies Governance Act
Maintain a central record of deployed AI and other Emerging Technologies systems requiring oversight.

summary.locator: page 81, 4.2.1, National AI and other Emerging Technologies Council
summary.quote: A statutory Council shall be established as the central regulatory authority for AI and other Emerging Technologies.
Oversee testing and evaluation of frontier AI models and significant AI risks relating to safety and security;

Establish the Kenya AI Safety Institute as the national technical institution responsible for AI safety research, testing, evaluation, benchmarking, red -teaming, incident analysis, and technical cooperation.
Establish an AI incident reporting framework for failures, harms, cybersecurity breaches
Promote age -appropriate, risk -based safeguards for child -facing AI and other Emerging Technologies systems.
Ensure that autonomous and semi-autonomous systems remain subject to meaningful human control, legal accountability, and applicable international law.

notes.quote: The Chairperson Committee on Artificial Intelligence and Other Emerging Technologies
It builds on existing foundations — including the Kenya AI Strategy (2025 –2030), the Digital Master Plan (2022 –2032), and the Data Protection Act (2019)
Office of the Attorney General to ensure consistency with Kenya’s constitutional framework

notes.locator: page 24, 1.5.5 Temporal Scope and Lifecycle Coverage
notes.quote: For systems placed into service after the effective date of this Policy, full compliance shall be required upon the coming into force of relevant implementing regulations.
For systems already in operation prior to the effective date (legacy systems), a transitional period of 2 years shall apply.
High-risk legacy systems shall achieve full compliance within three years.

judgment.status_reasoning: The ministry published the policy as a draft for public comment, with a submission deadline of 4 August 2026; the PDF itself describes 'the draft Policy' and a final validation through public participation. The comment period has closed by 18 Oct 2026, but nothing stored shows Cabinet approval, adoption as a sessional paper or a bill. Draft / proposed, legal force Proposed.
judgment.scope_reasoning: An AI-specific national governance policy with a risk-based regulatory framework, a safety institute and incident reporting; in scope with no note.
judgment.date_reasoning: The cover reads 'JULY 2026' and no day is given in the stored files; 2026-07 is kept.
judgment.topics_reasoning: Unchanged and supported: risk-based classification (3.5.2), safety institute (3.7.5 Kenya AI Safety Institute), incident reporting (3.7.5 incident reporting framework), evaluation & testing (testing and evaluation protocols for high-risk systems, red-teaming), human oversight (3.7.2), national security & military (3.7.6).
